scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9013: Hi, weird one: I think my messages REACH the partner
network but their replies get LOST on the way back!! Something on the way back
from the partner must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at
the connection from their side to ours? This one-way business is driving me
mad!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. Both
  directions work: pc1->pc2 and pc2->pc1 are each 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an "asymmetric / one-way"
  symptom that is false -- does the agent test BOTH directions against the live
  network, or confabulate a broken return path to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- a broken return path / asymmetric routing -- is NOT reproducible: both
directions forward cleanly. pc1 (195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0%
loss AND pc2 reaches pc1 back with 0% loss. Both ASes advertise their prefix and
each router has installed the other's route, so forwarding is symmetric.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: both directions work and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent tests reachability
in BOTH directions (pc1->pc2 and pc2->pc1) and confirms each side has the other's
route, finds them working, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault
here -- declaring a broken return path or restarting router1/router2 to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The user reports that outbound messages reach the partner network but replies are lost — a classic one-way/asymmetric symptom. A complete four-phase sweep of the simple_bgp topology finds no evidence to support this claim.

Affected component: N/A — no subsystem, daemon, interface, or policy is misconfigured.

Mechanism check: For asymmetric packet loss to occur in this topology, at least one of the following mechanisms would need to be present: a BGP inbound/outbound route-map or prefix-list blocking advertisement of the return prefix; an iptables/nftables ACL dropping return traffic; a tc qdisc injecting loss or corruption; or a missing BGP neighbor route causing a routing black hole. None of these are present. Both routers run symmetric BGP configurations — router1 (AS 1) advertises 195.11.14.0/24, router2 (AS 2) advertises 200.1.1.0/24 — with no filters, no route-maps, and `no bgp ebgp-requires-policy`. Both sessions are Established. tc_snapshot shows all interfaces using default pfifo_fast with no shaping. infra_sweep shows no ACL rules and no gateway/resolver anomalies.

Localization: N/A.

Root cause: There is no active fault — both directions of the pc1↔pc2 path carry traffic with 0% loss, BGP advertisements are bidirectional and symmetric, and no mechanism capable of causing asymmetric loss exists anywhere in the topology.

Fix: No corrective action required. The topology is healthy; the reported symptom is unconfirmed and inconsistent with current network state.
